methodology: Independently discovered from public web sources; normalized facts only. Admission remains separate.

events.subject: LME/SHFE/COMEX inventory divergence
events.fact: LME copper stocks were 244,025t versus about 400,000t in April; SHFE stocks about 69,300t versus above 430,000t in March; COMEX stocks 717,314 short tons on Aug 3. Chinese downstream consumption was reported weakening at higher prices.
events.effect_basis: Falling LME/SHFE availability is supportive, while rising COMEX stocks and weaker China downstream consumption offset a clean direction.

events.subject: DRC copper concentrate export ban
events.fact: DRC issued an immediate ban on copper and cobalt concentrate exports, while permitting one-year strategic waivers and with substantial domestic processing already present.
events.effect_basis: Immediate restriction can tighten tradable concentrate availability, but waivers/domestic processing reduce magnitude.

events.subject: DRC ban impact reassessment
events.fact: Follow-up analysis found limited likely global supply impact from the DRC ban because refined copper dominates exports, exemptions recur and domestic smelting capacity has expanded, while broader concentrate tightness and falling LME stocks persisted.
events.effect_basis: Downgrades the DRC-specific bullish shock but confirms broader raw-material tightness.
